## Solution

**Setup.** Let $\vec a, \vec b, \vec c$ be unit vectors with $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|=\sqrt 3$. Expanding,
$$|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|^2 = 3+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=3,$$
so, setting $p=\vec a\cdot\vec b,\; q=\vec b\cdot\vec c,\; r=\vec c\cdot\vec a$,
$$p+q+r=0. \tag{1}$$

**Reducing the expression.** Using the Lagrange identity $(\vec u\times\vec v)\cdot(\vec w\times\vec x)=(\vec u\cdot\vec w)(\vec v\cdot\vec x)-(\vec u\cdot\vec x)(\vec v\cdot\vec w)$:

$$
(\vec a\times\vec b)\cdot(\vec b\times\vec c)=(\vec a\cdot\vec b)(\vec b\cdot\vec c)-(\vec a\cdot\vec c)(\vec b\cdot\vec b)=pq-r,
$$
$$
(\vec b\times\vec c)\cdot(\vec c\times\vec a)=(\vec b\cdot\vec c)(\vec c\cdot\vec a)-(\vec b\cdot\vec a)(\vec c\cdot\vec c)=qr-p,
$$
$$
(\vec c\times\vec a)\cdot(\vec a\times\vec b)=(\vec c\cdot\vec a)(\vec a\cdot\vec b)-(\vec c\cdot\vec b)(\vec a\cdot\vec a)=rp-q.
$$

Summing and using (1):
$$
S=(pq+qr+rp)-(p+q+r)=pq+qr+rp.
$$

From $(p+q+r)^2=0=p^2+q^2+r^2+2(pq+qr+rp)$,
$$
S=pq+qr+rp=-\tfrac12(p^2+q^2+r^2)\le 0. \tag{2}
$$

**Attainability.** Equality in (2) requires $p=q=r=0$, i.e. three mutually orthogonal unit vectors. These exist in $\mathbb R^3$ (e.g. the standard basis), and they satisfy $p+q+r=0$, hence $|\vec a+\vec b+\vec c|=\sqrt 3$. For this choice each cross product is a unit vector orthogonal to the other two cross products, so every pairwise dot product of cross products is $0$, giving $S=0$ directly — consistent with (2).

**Conclusion.** The maximum value is

$$\boxed{0}.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
